title: RISE Live: a better voice under the same clock
acceptance: A provider text-to-speech renderer on the reader's own key is a sibling of the browser voice under the one clock (design §2.2 reason 4, §8 stage 7): the voice contract unchanged (attach/enqueue/hold/release/seek/setRate/cancel/close/playedMs), RISE's runtime the clock, the provider only rendering what RISE says when RISE says it.

Each passage is fetched as samples with character timestamps and played through Web Audio: a mark at the start of every word; an exact hold that stops the sound where it is and takes up from the same sample; a seek and a replay that play from what was fetched with no second request; the next passage fetched while this one plays.

The key is the reader's, typed into the venue, held in the page's memory only, sent in one header to the provider and nowhere else, never in a page, a log, About or an error; the venue says whose key the voice is on and that each passage's words go to the provider to be spoken; a question is refused until the key is typed.

A change of rate never interrupts a passage: the next is fetched at the provider's speed within what it takes (0.7 to 1.2) and the rest is made up by the playback rate; a provider refusal (key, credit, rate, network) fails the passage with the provider's reason in the reader's words and the reading goes on paced, as a browser passage fails.
About this reading names the voice, its model and the characters sent; the bed ducks under it as under the browser's voice; the card is untouched.
